title: Greetings & Introductions
description: Master essential everyday greetings, how to introduce yourself and others politely.

sections.title: Basic Greetings
sections.content: In English, greetings vary depending on the time of day and the degree of formality. Use "Good morning" before 12:00 PM, "Good afternoon" until approximately 5:00 PM, and "Good evening" afterwards.

examples.en: Hello, my name is Alex. Nice to meet you!
examples.ru: Здравствуйте, меня зовут Алекс. Приятно познакомиться!

examples.en: Good morning! How are you doing today?
examples.ru: Доброе утро! Как ваши дела сегодня?

sections.title: Asking Personal Information
sections.content: To inquire about someone’s name and origin, we use questions with question words like "What" and "Where". Remember to invert the subject and the verb "to be".

examples.en: Where are you from? — I am from London.
examples.ru: Откуда вы? — Я из Лондона.

examples.en: What is your job? — I am an engineer.
examples.ru: Кем вы работаете? — Я инженер.

exercises.question: Which greeting is appropriate at 9:00 AM in a formal setting?
exercises.explanation: Before 12:00 noon, the standard polite greeting is "Good morning".

exercises.question: Where ___ you from?
exercises.explanation: With the subject "you", the correct present form of the verb "to be" is "are".

title: Numbers, Time & Dates
description: Learn cardinal and ordinal numbers, telling time and expressing dates with accuracy.

sections.title: Cardinal vs Ordinal Numbers
sections.content: Cardinal numbers (one, two, three) express quantities, while ordinal numbers (first, second, third) show order or date sequence.

examples.en: I have two brothers and one sister.
examples.ru: У меня два брата и одна сестра.

examples.en: Today is the third of May.
examples.ru: Сегодня третье мая.

sections.title: Telling Time
sections.content: In standard British English, minutes before 30 use "past" (e.g., quarter past four), and after 30 use "to" (e.g., ten to six). In American English, "after" and "till/of" are also common.

examples.en: It is half past seven.
examples.ru: Половина восьмого.

examples.en: The train arrives at quarter to five.
examples.ru: Поезд прибывает без пятнадцати пять.

exercises.question: What is the correct ordinal form of the number 3?
exercises.explanation: The ordinal form of 3 is "third" (3rd).

exercises.question: How do you say 7:15 in spoken English?
exercises.explanation: 15 minutes after 7 is expressed as "quarter past seven" or "fifteen past seven".

title: Colors, Shapes & Everyday Objects
description: Build your vocabulary for describing common objects, clothing, and surroundings.

sections.title: Descriptive Adjectives
sections.content: Adjectives usually precede the noun they modify in English. For example, "a red car", not "a car red".

examples.en: She is wearing a blue jacket.
examples.ru: На ней надета синяя куртка.

examples.en: The table is round and wooden.
examples.ru: Стол круглый и деревянный.

exercises.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:
exercises.explanation: In English, attributive adjectives come immediately before the noun: "a black pen".

title: Family & Relationships
description: Learn terms for family members, possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her), and family trees.

sections.title: Possessive Adjectives and Genitive 's
sections.content: Use 's to indicate possession for people: "Mark's mother". Possessive determiners include my, your, his, her, its, our, their.

examples.en: This is my brother’s bicycle.
examples.ru: Это велосипед моего брата.

examples.en: Her parents live in a small village.
examples.ru: Её родители живут в небольшой деревне.

exercises.question: Which word completes: "Sarah is talking to ___ father"?
exercises.explanation: Since Sarah is female, the corresponding singular possessive adjective is "her".

title: Food, Drink & Ordering in Cafés
description: Basic food items, countable vs uncountable nouns, and ordering politeness.

sections.title: Polite Requests
sections.content: Rather than saying "I want", use "Could I please have..." or "I would like (I'd like)...".

examples.en: Could I have a cup of black coffee, please?
examples.ru: Можно мне чашку чёрного кофе, пожалуйста?

examples.en: I would like some orange juice.
examples.ru: Я бы хотел немного апельсинового сока.

exercises.question: What is the most polite way to order coffee in a cafe?
options: I would like a cup of coffee, please
exercises.correctAnswer: I would like a cup of coffee, please
exercises.explanation: "I would like..." followed by "please" is the accepted polite standard.

title: Shopping & Retail Transactions
description: Ask for prices, sizes, payment methods, and return policies in stores.

sections.title: How Much vs How Many
sections.content: Use "how much" with uncountable nouns (money, milk, information) and "how many" with countable plurals (apples, shirts, shoes).

examples.en: How much does this pair of trousers cost?
examples.ru: Сколько стоят эти брюки?

examples.en: How many bags do you need?
examples.ru: Сколько пакетов вам нужно?

exercises.question: Which question correctly asks for the price?
exercises.explanation: "How much is..." is the standard phrasing when asking for the cost of an item.

title: Travel, Directions & Transport
description: Navigate airports, train stations, and ask for directional landmarks.

sections.title: Prepositions of Movement and Place
sections.content: Common directional prepositions include: straight ahead, turn left, turn right, opposite, next to, between.

examples.en: Turn right at the traffic lights and go straight ahead.
examples.ru: Поверните направо на светофоре и идите прямо.

examples.en: The pharmacy is opposite the post office.
examples.ru: Аптека находится напротив почтового отделения.

exercises.question: Complete: "Go ___ ahead for 200 meters until you reach the bridge."
exercises.explanation: The idiom is "go straight ahead".

title: Weather & Seasonal Forecasts
description: Describe climatic conditions, temperatures, and seasonal activities.

sections.title: Weather Adjectives from Nouns
sections.content: Add -y to nouns: sun -> sunny, rain -> rainy, cloud -> cloudy, wind -> windy.

examples.en: It is chilly and windy today.
examples.ru: Сегодня прохладно и ветрено.

examples.en: The forecast predicts heavy snow tomorrow.
examples.ru: Прогноз обещает сильный снегопад завтра.

exercises.question: What is the adjective for "fog"?
exercises.explanation: The adjective for fog is "foggy" (with double g).

title: Health, Symptoms & Medical Visits
description: Express physical ailments, visit a doctor, and understand prescriptions.

sections.title: Expressing Pain and Illness
sections.content: Use "have got a headache / stomachache / sore throat" or "my [body part] hurts".

examples.en: I have had a high fever and a cough since yesterday.
examples.ru: У меня высокая температура и кашель со вчерашнего дня.

examples.en: Take this medicine twice a day after meals.
examples.ru: Принимайте это лекарство дважды в день после еды.

exercises.question: Which phrase is correct?
exercises.explanation: "A sore throat" is the standard collocated medical phrase.

title: Hobbies, Sports & Leisure Interests
description: Talk about free-time activities using gerunds and verbs of preference (enjoy, like, prefer).

sections.title: Verbs Followed by Gerunds (-ing)
sections.content: Verbs like enjoy, fancy, avoid, and keep are followed by the gerund (-ing form).

examples.en: She really enjoys painting landscapes at weekends.
examples.ru: Ей очень нравится рисовать пейзажи по выходным.

examples.en: Do you prefer playing football or watching it?
examples.ru: Ты предпочитаешь играть в футбол или смотреть его?

exercises.question: He enjoys ___ in the local park every morning.
exercises.explanation: The verb "enjoy" is followed by a gerund: "enjoys jogging".

title: Higher Education & Lifelong Learning
description: Discuss academic disciplines, university admissions, and modern pedagogical styles.

sections.title: Academic Terminology
sections.content: Understand the difference between undergraduate, postgraduate, curriculum, syllabus, and dissertations.

examples.en: He graduated with a bachelor’s degree in computer science.
examples.ru: Он получил степень бакалавра в области компьютерных наук.

examples.en: Students must submit their coursework before the deadline.
examples.ru: Студенты должны сдать свои курсовые работы до дедлайна.

exercises.question: What do we call a university degree obtained after a Bachelor's degree?
exercises.explanation: A Master's degree is a postgraduate qualification pursued after a Bachelor's.

title: Modern Workplace & Career Development
description: Job applications, cover letters, interviews, and professional correspondence.

sections.title: Present Perfect for Career Experience
sections.content: We use the Present Perfect (have/has + past participle) when discussing cumulative professional experience without specifying a closed past time.

examples.en: I have worked in project management for over five years.
examples.ru: Я работаю в сфере управления проектами более пяти лет.

examples.en: She has successfully spearheaded several marketing campaigns.
examples.ru: Она успешно возглавила несколько маркетинговых кампаний.

exercises.question: Which tense is best for stating non-time-specific past career achievements?
exercises.explanation: Present Perfect links past achievements to present relevance.

title: Environmental Sustainability & Climate
description: Ecology, biodiversity conservation, carbon footprint, and renewable resources.

sections.title: Cause and Effect Linkers
sections.content: Use cohesive devices: consequently, as a result of, lead to, stem from, therefore.

examples.en: Excessive emissions lead to global temperature rise.
examples.ru: Чрезмерные выбросы приводят к повышению глобальной температуры.

examples.en: Consequently, polar glaciers are receding at an alarming rate.
examples.ru: Следовательно, полярные ледники отступают с тревожной скоростью.

exercises.question: Choose the synonym for "as a consequence":
exercises.explanation: "Therefore" indicates a logical result or consequence.

title: Technology & Digital Transformation
description: Automation, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and digital ethics.

sections.title: Passive Voice in Technical Descriptions
sections.content: Technical writing favors the passive voice to maintain an objective tone: subject + to be + past participle.

examples.en: Sensitive data is encrypted using 256-bit protocols.
examples.ru: Конфиденциальные данные шифруются с использованием 256-битных протоколов.

exercises.question: Change into passive: "Engineers develop automated software."
options: Automated software is developed by engineers.
Software has been develop by engineers.
exercises.correctAnswer: Automated software is developed by engineers.
exercises.explanation: The object "Automated software" becomes the subject with "is developed".

title: Culture, Traditions & Global Heritage
description: Cross-cultural communication, intercultural sensitivity, and world traditions.

sections.title: Modal Verbs of Obligation and Advice
sections.content: Use should, ought to, must, have to, and needn't appropriately.

examples.en: Travelers should respect local traditions when visiting religious monuments.
examples.ru: Путешественникам следует уважать местные традиции при посещении религиозных памятников.

exercises.question: Which modal verb expresses strong internal moral obligation?
exercises.explanation: "Must" conveys necessity or strong moral conviction.

title: Mass Media & Information Literacy
description: Analyze bias in news journalism, algorithmic bubbles, and fact-checking mechanisms.

sections.title: Nuanced Vocabulary of Journalism
sections.content: Terms like sensationalism, editorial neutrality, misinformation, disinformation, and confirmation bias.

examples.en: Echo chambers reinforce preconceived cognitive biases among social media audiences.
examples.ru: Эхо-камеры усиливают предвзятость мышления у аудитории социальных сетей.

exercises.question: What term describes deliberately deceptive information designed to manipulate public opinion?
exercises.explanation: "Disinformation" refers specifically to intentionally fabricated deception.

title: Scientific Frontiers & Bioethics
description: Genetic editing (CRISPR), bioethical debates, and clinical trial methodologies.

sections.title: Hypothetical and Conditional Structures
sections.content: Master mixed conditionals (e.g., If scientists had not mapped the genome, certain therapies would not exist today).

examples.en: Were gene therapy to become affordable, genetic diseases could be largely eradicated.
examples.ru: Если бы генная терапия стала доступной, генетические заболевания можно было бы практически искоренить.

exercises.question: Identify the inverted formal conditional: "If we should require more evidence..."
exercises.explanation: Inversion of "If we should require" drops "if" and starts with "Should we require".

title: Political Science & Civic Governance
description: Democracy, international treaties, separation of powers, and civic responsibilities.

sections.title: Formal Academic Collocations
sections.content: Implement legislation, ratify international conventions, exercise constitutional authority, ensure transparency.

examples.en: The general assembly convened to ratify the landmark climate accords.
examples.ru: Генеральная ассамблея собралась для ратификации эпохальных климатических соглашений.

exercises.question: Which verb naturally collocates with "a treaty"?
exercises.explanation: Countries "ratify" treaties or international agreements.

title: Economics, Fiscal Policy & Markets
description: Inflation, supply chain resilience, central bank interest rates, and macroeconomics.

sections.title: Hedging and Cautionary Language
sections.content: Academic English avoids dogmatic assertions through epistemic verbs (tend to, suggest, indicate, appear to).

examples.en: The empirical data appears to indicate a gradual deceleration in domestic consumption.
examples.ru: Эмпирические данные, по-видимому, указывают на постепенное замедление внутреннего потребления.

exercises.question: Which sentence demonstrates appropriate academic hedging?
options: High interest rates always destroy the economy completely.
Elevated interest rates tend to exert downward pressure on consumer borrowing.
exercises.correctAnswer: Elevated interest rates tend to exert downward pressure on consumer borrowing.
exercises.explanation: "Tend to exert" shows measured, cautious academic tone.

title: Cognitive Psychology & Human Behavior
description: Behavioral conditioning, cognitive dissonance, emotional intelligence, and memory models.

sections.title: Cleft Sentences for Emphasis
sections.content: Use "It was X that...", "What surprised researchers was...", "The reason why..." to emphasize key findings.

examples.en: What psychologists observed was a substantial decline in impulsive responses.
examples.ru: То, что наблюдали психологи, было существенным снижением импульсивных реакций.

exercises.question: Transform for emphasis: "The lack of sleep caused the deficit." -> "What caused the deficit was ___"
exercises.explanation: The wh-cleft structure is: What [verb phrase] was [focal noun phrase].

title: Epistemology & Moral Philosophy
description: Examine ethical dilemmas, utilitarianism versus deontology, and theories of truth.

sections.title: Philosophical Discourse
sections.content: Discuss axiomatic principles, categorical imperatives, empirical verification, and existential determinism.

examples.en: Deontological ethics posits that actions possess intrinsic moral worth regardless of teleological outcomes.
examples.ru: Деонтологическая этика утверждает, что поступки обладают внутренней моральной ценностью независимо от телеологических результатов.

exercises.question: Which philosophical paradigm judges the moral rectitude of an act solely by its ultimate consequences?
exercises.explanation: Consequentialism and utilitarianism hold that consequences determine moral worth.

title: Jurisprudence & Constitutional Law
description: Statutory interpretation, legal precedents, habeas corpus, and judicial review.

sections.title: Legal Registers and Latinate Terminology
sections.content: Understand terms such as prima facie, stare decisis, bona fide, jurisdiction, and appellant jurisprudence.

examples.en: The appellate court upheld the doctrine of stare decisis, deferring to established judicial precedent.
examples.ru: Апелляционный суд поддержал доктрину stare decisis, сославшись на установленный судебный прецедент.

exercises.question: What does the legal maxim "stare decisis" instruct judges to do?
options: Stand by precedents and previously decided cases
exercises.correctAnswer: Stand by precedents and previously decided cases
exercises.explanation: Stare decisis is the legal principle of determining points in litigation according to precedent.

title: Advanced Medical Research & Oncology
description: Cellular senescence, oncogenes, targeted immunotherapy, and randomized double-blind clinical trials.

sections.title: Complex Nominalization in Scientific Writing
sections.content: Nominalization condenses ideas by converting verbs and adjectives into concise nouns (e.g., proliferate -> cellular proliferation).

examples.en: The inhibition of telomerase activity hampers neoplastic cellular proliferation.
examples.ru: Ингибирование активности теломеразы препятствует опухолевой клеточной пролиферации.

exercises.question: Select the nominalized form of "The cells mutated rapidly, which hindered the treatment":
options: Rapid cellular mutation hindered the therapeutic intervention.
Cells mutated and this was bad for treatment.
Treatment stopped because cells were mutating fast.
Because mutating cells happened, treatment failed.
exercises.correctAnswer: Rapid cellular mutation hindered the therapeutic intervention.
exercises.explanation: Converting verbs to abstract noun phrases creates authoritative scientific prose.

title: Empirical Research Methodologies & Statistics
description: Statistical significance, p-values, qualitative ethnography, and meta-analytic synthesis.

sections.title: Statistical Reporting and Rigor
sections.content: Master phrases such as "statistically significant at the 95% confidence interval", "confounding variables", and "spurious correlation".

examples.en: Multivariate regression analysis revealed that socioeconomic status was a confounding variable.
examples.ru: Многомерный регрессионный анализ показал, что социально-экономический статус был вмешивающейся переменной.

exercises.question: What term defines an unmeasured extraneous variable that correlates with both independent and dependent variables?
exercises.explanation: A confounder distorts the perceived relationship between the primary variables.

title: International Diplomacy & Geopolitics
description: Multilateral treaties, soft power, deterrence doctrine, and international arbitration.

sections.title: Diplomatic Subtlety and Understatement
sections.content: Diplomatic communique utilizes measured understatement and diplomatic equivocation to avert escalation.

examples.en: The foreign ministry expressed grave reservations regarding unilateral cross-border incursions.
examples.ru: Министерство иностранных дел выразило серьёзную озабоченность по поводу односторонних трансграничных вторжений.

exercises.question: What diplomatic phrase communicates profound formal disapproval without declaring war?
options: To express grave reservations / profound concern
exercises.correctAnswer: To express grave reservations / profound concern
exercises.explanation: "Grave reservations" is the diplomatic standard for deep opposition.

title: Theoretical Linguistics & Semiotics
description: Morphosyntax, generative grammar, phonological assimilation, and Saussurean semiotics.

sections.title: Signifier and Signified
sections.content: Ferdinand de Saussure conceptualized language as an arbitrary system of signs comprised of the signifier (acoustic sound-image) and the signified (mental concept).

examples.en: The arbitrariness of the linguistic sign underscores the conventional nature of communicative codes.
examples.ru: Произвольность языкового знака подчёркивает конвенциональную природу коммуникативных кодов.

exercises.question: In Saussurean linguistics, what constitutes the "signifier"?
options: The acoustic sound-image or visual form
The physical referent in the real world
exercises.correctAnswer: The acoustic sound-image or visual form
exercises.explanation: The signifier is the form which the sign takes, whereas the signified is the concept it represents.

title: Advanced Literary Criticism & Hermeneutics
description: Post-structuralism, deconstruction, narrative voice, and intertextuality in classic literature.

sections.title: Hermeneutic Analysis
sections.content: Hermeneutics explores the iterative process of textual interpretation, emphasizing the historical hermeneutic circle between parts and the whole.

examples.en: Derridean deconstruction exposes the internal contradictions and aporias inherent within metaphysical texts.
examples.ru: Дерридианская деконструкция вскрывает внутренние противоречия и апории, присущие метафизическим текстам.

exercises.question: What rhetorical term denotes an irresolvable internal contradiction or impasse in philosophical prose?
exercises.explanation: An aporia is an impasse or paradoxical perplexity in philosophical reasoning.

title: Classical Rhetoric & Oratorical Persuasion
description: Ethos, pathos, logos, chiasmus, zeugma, litotes, and masterclass persuasive techniques.

sections.title: Sophisticated Rhetorical Tropes
sections.content: Chiasmus (criss-cross structure), Zeugma (one verb governing disparate clauses), and Litotes (ironic double negative).

examples.en: She opened her heart and her wallet to the orphan (Zeugma).
examples.ru: Она открыла сироте и сердце, и кошелёк (Зевгма).

examples.en: He is not without intellectual merit (Litotes).
examples.ru: Он вовсе не лишён интеллектуальных достоинств (Литота).

exercises.question: Which sentence exemplifies litotes?
options: The performance was not entirely unsatisfactory.
He ran like a cheetah through the savanna.
Boom! went the fireworks in the night.
exercises.correctAnswer: The performance was not entirely unsatisfactory.
exercises.explanation: Litotes employs deliberate understatement through double negatives.

title: Critical Epistemic Analysis & Fallacies
description: Detect cognitive sophistry, ad hominem, strawman arguments, and tautological deductions.

sections.title: Dissecting Fallacious Arguments
sections.content: Rigorous debate demands identifying non sequitur, false dichotomies, and slippery slope fallacies in policy proposals.

examples.en: To conflate correlation with causation represents an egregious empirical fallacy.
examples.ru: Смешивать корреляцию с причинно-следственной связью представляет собой вопиющую эмпирическую ошибку.

exercises.question: What fallacy occurs when an opponent attacks the individual instead of addressing their substantive thesis?
exercises.explanation: Argumentum ad hominem attacks the character of the speaker rather than the argument.

title: Mastery of Scholarly Academic Prose
description: Publishing in peer-reviewed journals, syntactic elegance, cohesion, and scholarly peer reviews.

sections.title: Stylistic Panache and Syntactic Fluidity
sections.content: At the C2 proficiency echelon, prose combines rhythmic sentence variation, periodic sentence climaxes, and flawless idiomatic cadence.

examples.en: Far from being a mere pedagogical luxury, rigorous academic writing crystallizes disciplined thought.
examples.ru: Будучи далеко не просто педагогической роскошью, строгое академическое письмо кристаллизует дисциплинированное мышление.

exercises.question: Which transitional device best bridges two opposing scholarly viewpoints with supreme elegance?
options: Notwithstanding these caveats, an alternative paradigm emerges
On the other side of things
exercises.correctAnswer: Notwithstanding these caveats, an alternative paradigm emerges
exercises.explanation: This phrase captures the highest standard of academic synthesis.
